titles.595: Annotatio IV §.XX open: Danhauer and Strauch try to claim Waldenses as Lutheran Supper allies
titles.596: Annotatio IV §.XX: (1) They admit Waldensian confession unclear — thanksgiving/commemoration; Picard obscurity
titles.597: Annotatio IV §.XX: (2–3) Silence spiritual-mode half; Strauch despairs — organ of eating usually named Faith
titles.598: Annotatio IV §.XX: Taborite ‘with/in bread’ formulas seem Lutheran In/Cum/Sub — but Hoc is bread only
titles.599: Annotatio IV §.XX: presence only SACRAMENTALLY AND SPIRITUALLY — ‘here or there’ corporal claim = false prophets
titles.600: Annotatio IV §.XX close: in sacrament SPIRITUALLY not corporally; Calixtus — they denied true-body presence — stop before §.XXI

latin.595: §. XX. Et hæc est causa quare Biga Clarissimorum Theologorum Lutheranorum, JOHANNES CONRADUS DANHAUERUS Argentoratensis, & ÆGIDIUS STRAUCHIUS Wittebergensis, in suis, de Waldensium Ecclesia, Dissertationibus, horum, cum sua, de S. Cœna, fide, conciliatura & Waldenses Lutheranæ fidei testes & socios ostensura,
latin.596: (1) tamen fateri necesse habet, minus claram esse Waldensium Confessionem, quæ apud Sleidanum extet lib. 16. puta, eam in partem, claram, ut cum Lutherana videri possit eadem, quia dicunt: Esse S. Cœnam gratiarum actionem & beneficii per Christum accepti commemorationem. Imò verò Strauchius Aphorismum suum 10, capitis secundi, ita format: De Cœna Domini minùs certum est, quid omnes (Waldenses) sentiant, ac multo minus quid olim senserint: Quamvis enim Picardi orthodoxè articulum hunc exponere videantur, aliorum tamen Confessiones obscuriores sunt, quàm ut Zwinglianismum in iisdem damnari luculenter appareat.
latin.597: (2) Introductura eam Confessionis Waldensium partem, quâ Corporis Christi in Cœna præsentiam isti profitentur, à Reformatis non minùs quàm Lutheranis admissam, alteram tamen Confessionis partem, quâ præsentiæ hujus modum ubique deprædicant Spiritualem, corporali oppositum, alto silentio involvit Danhauerus §. 31. & Strauchius cit. aphorism. in ekthesei §. 1. (3) Organon manducationis corporis Christi ex mente Waldensium expositurus Strauchius, de Waldensium cum Lutheranis Consensu planè desperat, ita §. 2. scribens: Cæterùm cum in aliis Waldensium Confessionibus obscuriuscule exponatur sacramentorum doctrina, & organon participandi rei cælestis plerumque FIDES nominetur, aliorum sit de Orthodoxia Waldensium Neotericorum, & imprimis eorum qui Calvinianorum tutelam implorant, judicium &c. &c.
latin.598: Equidem pro Consensu Waldensium Juniorum cum Lutheranis in puncto de S. Cœna, introduci posset, Articulus primus Taboritarum contra Papistas Pragenses de præsentia & adoratione Christi in Sacramento, à neutro licet Theologorum binorum, in Dissertationibus eorum notatus, quô expressè perhibent: Cum pane verè esse corpus Christi de Virgine sumtum pro nobis traditum. Item: Corpus Christi in pane esse: Quæ duæ formulæ dicendi exactè respondent tô In, Cum, & Sub Lutherano. At (1) In eodem articulo contendunt Taboritæ, pronomen, Hoc, in propositione Christi: hoc est Corpus meum, aliud nihil, quàm panem demonstrare, id quod à mente Lutheranorum modernorum omnino alienum est.
latin.599: (2) Addunt, cum & in pane, esse tantum SACRAMENTALITER ET SPIRITUALITER, non autem communibus proprietatibus, tam essentialibus, quàm Accidentalibus consequentibus, quale tantùm ad dextram patris in Cœlo sit & ad quod omnis fidelis in mente debeat attendere, suspensâ consideratione circa naturam Materialis substantiæ sacramenti: Disertius adhuc idem, paulò post verba, à Danhauero, pro Waldensium cum Lutheranis consensu, in medium adducta, ita profitentes; Annon Christus ipsemet eos qui eum, post abitum illius corporalem, in terris corporaliter præsentem profitentur, dicentes, hic aut illic (in pane) est Christus, vocat Pseudoprophetas, à quibus diligenter cavendis suos præmonet. (3) Esse in pane Corpus Christi, tantum non innumeris in locis exponunt per tô esse corpus Christi in Sacramento SPIRITUALITER.
latin.600: Audiamus illos loquentes…: In Sacramentis verò est, inquiunt, Corpus Christi… atque hinc est ut in sacramentis profiteamur Christum esse non PERSONALITER aut CORPORALITER, sive SENSIBILITER nostris sensibus ac corpori, sed solum essendi MODO jam dicto SPIRITUALI… utrobique SPIRITUALITER, POTENTIA SCIL. SUA AC EFICACIA, HIC OPERANDO SALUTEM OMNI CREDENTI… Christus adsit in Sacramento NON CORPORALITER ac sensibiliter corpori nostro, sed MODO ESSENDI SUO SPIRITUALI… Nec est cur Ægidius Strauchius… dicat: Optandum esse ut haberemus antiquorum Waldensium genuinam Confessionem… Nam & hanc, ex parte saltem, habemus, istamque partem adduximus suprà §. 16., Lutheranæ Sententiæ è diametro adversam. Ut permotus videatur hôc ipsô B. Georgius Calixtus…: Waldenses, inquit, sive Picardos Bohemiæ & Moraviæ, præsentiam veri Corporis in Eucharistia, negasse notum est.

pass_a.595: §. XX. And this is the cause why a Pair of most Famous Lutheran Theologians — JOHANNES CONRADUS DANHAUER of Strasbourg and ÆGIDIUS STRAUCH of Wittenberg — in their Dissertations on the Waldensian Church, about to reconcile these with their own faith concerning the Sacred Supper and to show the Waldenses as witnesses and allies of the Lutheran faith,
pass_a.596: (1) yet is forced to confess that the Waldenses’ Confession which exists in Sleidanus Book 16 is less clear — namely that part clear enough that it could seem the same as the Lutheran — because they say: The Sacred Supper is a thanksgiving and a commemoration of the benefit received through Christ. Nay indeed Strauch forms his 10th Aphorism of the second chapter thus: Concerning the Lord’s Supper it is less certain what all (Waldenses) sense, and much less what they formerly sensed: For although the Picards seem to expound this article orthodoxly, yet others’ Confessions are more obscure than that Zwinglianism should lucidly appear condemned in the same.
pass_a.597: (2) About to introduce that part of the Waldenses’ Confession by which they profess the presence of Christ’s Body in the Supper — admitted by the Reformed no less than by Lutherans — yet Danhauer §. 31 and Strauch in the cited aphorism in the ekthesis §. 1 wrap in deep silence the other part of the Confession, by which everywhere they proclaim the mode of this presence Spiritual, opposed to the corporal. (3) About to expound from the Waldenses’ mind the organ of eating Christ’s body, Strauch plainly despairs of the Waldenses’ Consensus with the Lutherans, writing thus in §. 2: But for the rest, since in other Waldensian Confessions the doctrine of the sacraments is expounded rather obscurely, and the organ of participating in the heavenly thing is most often named FAITH, let others’ judgment be concerning the Orthodoxy of the Neoteric Waldenses, and especially of those who implore the Calvinists’ protection, &c. &c.
pass_a.598: Indeed for the Consensus of the Younger Waldenses with the Lutherans on the point of the Sacred Supper there could be introduced the Taborites’ first Article against the Prague Papists on the presence and adoration of Christ in the Sacrament — noted by neither of the pair of Theologians in their Dissertations — by which they expressly affirm: With the bread truly to be the body of Christ taken from the Virgin and handed over for us. Likewise: Christ’s Body to be in the bread: Which two formulas of speaking answer exactly to the Lutheran In, Cum, and Sub. But (1) In the same article the Taborites contend that the pronoun This in Christ’s proposition This is my Body demonstrates nothing other than the bread — which is altogether alien from the mind of modern Lutherans.
pass_a.599: (2) They add that with and in the bread it is only SACRAMENTALLY AND SPIRITUALLY, not however with the common essential and Accidental properties following — such as is only at the Father’s right in Heaven and to which every faithful ought to attend in mind, consideration of the Material substance of the sacrament suspended: Still more expressly the same, a little after the words Danhauer brought into the midst for Waldenses’ consensus with Lutherans, professing thus; Does not Christ Himself call those who after His corporal departure profess Him corporally present on earth, saying Here or there (in the bread) is Christ, Pseudoprophets, from whom He forewarns His own carefully to beware? (3) To be Christ’s Body in the bread they almost countless times expound by tô to be Christ’s body in the Sacrament SPIRITUALLY.
pass_a.600: Let us hear them speaking…: But in the Sacraments, they say, is Christ’s Body… and hence it is that in the sacraments we profess Christ to be not PERSONALLY or CORPORALLY, or SENSIBLY to our senses and body, but only in the SPIRITUAL mode of being already said… everywhere SPIRITUALLY, namely by HIS POWER AND EFFICACY, HERE WORKING SALVATION FOR EVERY BELIEVER… Christ is present in the Sacrament NOT CORPORALLY and sensibly to our body, but in HIS SPIRITUAL MODE OF BEING… Nor is there cause for Ægidius Strauch… to say: It were to be wished we had the genuine Confession of the ancient Waldenses… For we have this too, at least in part, and that part we brought above in §. 16., diametrically opposed to the Lutheran Sentence. So that blessed Georg Calixtus seems moved by this very thing to write of the Waldenses, even if not sufficiently knowing their sentence: The Waldenses, he says, or Picards of Bohemia and Moravia, are known to have denied the presence of the true Body in the Eucharist.

595: §.XX: this is why two famous Lutheran theologians — DANHAUER of Strasbourg and STRAUCH of Wittenberg — write dissertations on the Waldensian Church.
They mean to reconcile the Waldenses with their own Supper faith and show them as witnesses and allies of the Lutheran faith.
596: (1) Yet they must admit the Waldensian Confession in Sleidanus Book 16 is less clear than a Lutheran twin — it calls the Supper thanksgiving and commemoration of the benefit received through Christ.

Strauch’s Aphorism 10: less certain what all Waldenses sense, still less what they once sensed — Picards may look orthodox, but other confessions are too obscure for Zwinglianism to appear lucidly condemned.
597: (2) Danhauer and Strauch parade the confession’s presence half (admitted by Reformed and Lutheran alike) but wrap in deep silence the half that everywhere preaches the mode as Spiritual, opposed to corporal.

(3) On the organ of eating, Strauch plainly despairs of Lutheran consensus — other confessions obscurely name FAITH as the organ of sharing the heavenly thing; let others judge neoteric Waldenses who seek Calvinist protection.
598: A Taborite article neither Danhauer nor Strauch noted could seem to serve junior-Waldenses–Lutheran consensus: ‘with the bread truly Christ’s body’ and ‘Christ’s body in the bread’ — formulas matching Lutheran In, Cum, and Sub.
But (1) in the same article the Taborites make Hoc in ‘This is my Body’ point to nothing but the bread — wholly alien to the modern Lutheran mind.
599: (2) With and in the bread the body is only SACRAMENTALLY AND SPIRITUALLY — not with heaven’s essential/accidental properties; the faithful mind attends to what is at the Father’s right, suspending material-substance fixation.

After Danhauer’s ‘consensus’ quotes they add: those who after Christ’s corporal departure say ‘here or there (in the bread) is Christ’ He Himself calls false prophets. (3) ‘Body in the bread’ they almost endlessly gloss as body in the Sacrament SPIRITUALLY.
600: Hear them: in the sacraments Christ’s Body is present — not PERSONALLY, CORPORALLY, or SENSIBLY to our body, but only in the SPIRITUAL mode of being, by power and efficacy working salvation for every believer.

Strauch need not wish for an ancient Waldensian confession — we already have part of it above (§.16), diametrically against the Lutheran sentence; Calixtus notes the Bohemian/Moravian Picards denied true-Body presence in the Eucharist. Stop before §.XXI.
